label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
**One star for now: unresolved circulation failure and inadequate support**

Bridger Bend Community Library is a one-branch library with two full-time staff, volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. We signed a three-year contract with Stackhouse Cloud in June 2026 at $14,200 per year. Our migration went live October 19.

Since October 28, our checkouts have worked only in offline mode on one laptop. Approximately 640 holds disappeared from our holds queue. Our support ticket has been open for 12 days. We have received three replies, each saying the issue has been “escalated to engineering.” We still do not have a resolution or a clear timetable.

These failures have consequences beyond an inconvenient workday. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to collect the large-print Westerns he had placed on hold. We had no record of his hold and sent him home empty-handed. One of our volunteers has been recording checkouts on index cards. With our staffing, we cannot absorb this much extra work without taking time away from patrons.

During sales, we were promised “a dedicated migration specialist.” Our experience has instead been a shared inbox. That gap between the promised support and the support delivered is central to this review.

To be fair, the software looked good in the demo, and the staff interface is genuinely better than our previous system. My concern is not the product idea. It is the lack of effective support when essential services fail.

Our county budget hearing is November 18, and the library’s funding is on the agenda. We need concrete answers we can responsibly give our commissioners.

I am asking for a named senior person at Stackhouse to call me this week, take responsibility for coordinating the response, and provide a written recovery plan covering circulation and the missing holds.

For other small-library directors: get support response times, escalation procedures, and migration staffing commitments in writing before signing.

One star reflects our experience today. I will revisit this review if Stackhouse resolves these problems and follows through on support.
